title: Quran Study 64: Sura 2, the Qiblah, Steadfastness, Testing, and Safa and Marwah (1982-11-26)
date_note: Explicit in the filename. The file begins mid-discussion.
source_file: data/sources/playlists/audio-transcripts/64 - Friday Sermon 26 Nov 1982 By Dr Rashad Khalifa.csv
document_summary: A same-date companion to Study 62 that begins mid-discussion of mosques, Quran-alone preaching, the God-alone testimony, and the accumulated growth of tradition around the Quran. The group then conducts an extended qiblah debate using Quran 2:144–151, maps, compass directions, globe geometry, and the orientation of Tucson mosques. Quran 2:153–157 introduces steadfastness, martyrs alive with God, fear, hunger, loss, disaster, and the claim that believers should retain happiness through every circumstance. Personal letters and experiences are used to test the concept. The final block studies Safa and Marwah, Hagar's search for water, Hajj as an Abrahamic practice, and the distinction between obeying a ritual command and idolizing a place.

Quran 2:144–152 is read concerning facing the Sacred Mosque, opposition from previous scripture communities, competing directions, remembrance, and gratitude.

sections.title: Quran 2:153–157, steadfastness, martyrs alive, fear, hunger, loss, and perfect happiness
sections.summary: Quran 2:153–157 calls for steadfastness and prayer, describes those killed in God's cause as alive, and announces tests involving fear, hunger, money, lives, and crops. Rashad says the test reveals whether a person remains happy and convinced of God's mastery through success, failure, health, sickness, or loss.

related_questions: Which tests are listed in Quran 2:155?
What did he claim about happiness through hardship?

sections.title: Quran 2:158–163, Safa and Marwah, Hagar, Hajj, ritual obedience, and one God
sections.summary: Quran 2:158 introduces Safa and Marwah. Rashad traces the practice to Hagar's search for water and says Hajj and its rites came through Abraham. The group asks why traversing the hills is permitted if stones and places can become idols. Rashad distinguishes obeying God's command from worshiping the Kaaba or hills. The recording approaches Quran 2:163's declaration that the community's god is one God.
